name: cloakbrowser
description: CloakBrowser stealth Chromium through the Playwright MCP tool contract, via cloakbrowser-mcp. Its camoufox engine runs through a plugin-owned overlay that restores the stock search engines (Google by default).

headless.title: Headless
headless.description:
Run the browser without a window.

Default: false

Notes:
  - Headed mode is measurably less detectable, so leave this off unless you need a
    server with no display.
  - The launchers write the effective value explicitly: a missing or unsubstituted
    value means headed (false), never the engine's own headless default, and
    browser_capabilities reports the branch it took under launcherSettings.

browser_engine.title: Browser engine
browser_engine.description:
Which browser engine the plugin starts.

Options:
  - cloak — the patched CloakBrowser Chromium, with the stealth patches.
  - playwright — the stock Playwright Chromium; gives up the stealth patches.
  - camoufox — the Camoufox stealth Firefox; needs Python 3.12+ with uv installed.
  - camoufox-native — the user-installed mcp-camoufox package, with its own 27-tool
    contract and portable by default; install it yourself, the plugin does not bundle
    it.
  - kameleo — attaches to a running Kameleo Chroma profile over CDP; needs the Kameleo
    app with an active licence and a profile ID.

Default: cloak

Notes:
  - Junglefox profiles cannot be attached, and stealth over attach is unverified.
  - The engine is read when the MCP server starts; changing it restarts the server and
    reloads the tool list.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

tool_profile.title: Tool profile
tool_profile.description:
Which tools the selected engine exposes.

Options:
  - default — follows the engine manifest: full for cloak and playwright (the
    current 77-tool surface); portable for camoufox, camoufox-native and kameleo (a
    shared 24-tool core).
  - portable — the shared 24-tool core; hides engine-specific and extra tools.
  - full — everything the engine supports.

Default: default

Notes:
  - The seven tool groups and disabled_tools still apply.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

camoufox_profile.title: Camoufox native profile
camoufox_profile.description:
Profile name for the camoufox-native engine; one name per account.
Cookies and logins are kept under this name.

Default: default

Notes:
  - Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only, starting with a letter or
    digit, up to 64 characters.
  - A second Claude Code session using the same name is refused by the
    engine.

camoufox_data_dir.title: Camoufox native data directory
camoufox_data_dir.description:
Where the camoufox-native engine keeps its profiles and logs.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty for Claude Code's plugin data directory
    (profiles/camoufox-native).
  - Each profile is a 'profiles/<name>' folder inside it.
  - Use one directory per set of accounts.

kameleo_profile_id.title: Kameleo profile ID
kameleo_profile_id.description:
Profile ID to attach to. Required when the browser engine is kameleo.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Open Kameleo, create or start the profile, and copy its ID from the
    profile row.
  - The plugin never starts the Kameleo app; it connects to Kameleo's
    local API, which starts the profile.
  - Chromium (Chroma) profiles only: a Junglefox profile cannot be
    attached over CDP.

kameleo_endpoint.title: Kameleo CDP endpoint (optional)
kameleo_endpoint.description:
Full WebSocket CDP endpoint for the Kameleo profile.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty to use ws://127.0.0.1:5050/playwright/<profile ID>.
  - Only ws:// or wss:// on a loopback host is accepted; a non-loopback
    endpoint is rejected.

tools_vision.title: Mouse primitives (vision)
tools_vision.description:
Six coordinate mouse tools: click, move, drag, down, up and wheel.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes all six of them.

tools_pdf.title: PDF export
tools_pdf.description:
PDF export through browser_pdf_save.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes PDF export.

tools_devtools.title: Tracing, video and highlights
tools_devtools.description:
Thirteen devtools tools: tracing, video, recording, annotations and element
highlights.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes all thirteen of them.

tools_storage.title: Cookies and web storage
tools_storage.description:
Seventeen storage tools: cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage and storage
state.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes all seventeen of them.

tools_network.title: Network routing
tools_network.description:
Four network tools: route, unroute, route list and network state.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes request interception.

tools_testing.title: Assertions and locator generation
tools_testing.description:
Five testing tools: generate_locator and the four verify_* assertions.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes all five of them.

tools_config.title: Configuration read
tools_config.description:
Configuration introspection through browser_get_config.

Default: true

Notes:
  - Off removes that tool.

disabled_tools.title: Disabled tools
disabled_tools.description:
Comma-separated tool names to hide from the agent and reject when called.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - For example browser_pdf_save,browser_start_video.
  - Leave empty to expose the selected profile unchanged.

humanize.title: Humanised input
humanize.description:
Human-like mouse paths, keystroke timing and scrolling instead of
instant synthetic events.

Default: true

human_preset.title: Humanised input preset
human_preset.description:
How deliberate the humanised input is.

Options:
  - default — the normal humanised behaviour.
  - careful — slower and more deliberate.

Default: default

release_channel.title: Engine release channel
release_channel.description:
Which CloakBrowser release channel the engine uses.

Options:
  - stable — the free channel.
  - preview — requires a CloakBrowser Pro licence.

Default: stable

geoip_proxy_match.title: Match timezone and locale to the proxy
geoip_proxy_match.description:
Resolve the proxy exit location and align the browser timezone and locale
to it.

Default: false

Notes:
  - Enable this together with a proxy server.

profile_isolation.title: Profile isolation
profile_isolation.description:
Session safety for the browser profile: which profile a session uses and what it
leaves behind.

Options:
  - shared — one profile per account for every Claude Code window, exactly as
    before.
  - workspace — each project folder gets its own profile (profiles/<engine>/ws-<hash>),
    so two projects do not collide.
    That profile starts with a fresh login state, and if it is already in use the
    plugin uses a numbered sibling (ws-<hash>-2 to -5) and reports the switch.
  - isolated — no browser profile at all: no profile directory is created or
    locked, cookies, logins and storage are not saved, and nothing persists after
    the session.
    Profile directory, Account profile and the default-profile pointer are ignored
    and reported for that start, and several sessions can run at once.
  - copy — the session runs on a temporary copy of the profile that Profile
    directory, Account profile, the default-profile pointer or the engine default
    resolves.
    The base profile is locked for the session and never written, the browser
    starts on the copy, and the copy is discarded when the session ends cleanly.
    A crashed session leaves it under profiles/<engine>/.sessions, where
    browser_profiles list shows it and scripts/profile-copy.mjs --prune removes it.
  - copy-keep — the same temporary copy, and the changes are kept: when the session
    ends cleanly the base profile is replaced by the session copy and the old base
    is retained beside it as <name>.previous-<timestamp>.
    Those retained trees are never deleted automatically and accumulate until you
    remove them.
    A crash or a hard kill performs no swap: the base stays untouched and the
    session copy is kept.

Default: shared

Notes:
  - copy-keep is refused when the base is outside the plugin data directory.
  - copy does not combine with workspace in this version, and neither does copy-keep.
  - In shared, workspace, copy and copy-keep, Profile directory and Account profile
    win over the mode.
  - Only profiles the plugin manages are copied, given siblings or made isolated.
  - An explicit Profile directory keeps the block behaviour.
  - The free CloakBrowser tier still allows one browser at a time.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

on_locked.title: When the profile is in use
on_locked.description:
What this session does when the browser profile it resolved is already in use by
another process.

Options:
  - copy — this session runs on a temporary copy of the busy profile: the base keeps
    its owner and is never written, the copy takes no lock of its own, and it is
    deleted when your browser closes (profile_lifetime browser) or when the session
    ends.
    It carries that profile's cookies and saved logins as of the moment it is taken,
    and copy_contents decides how much of the rest travels with it.
    On an engine with a seat limit (the free CloakBrowser tier) a copy is still one
    browser at a time: the seat is checked again when the copy is actually taken, and
    when no seat is free this session holds and retries instead of starting a second
    browser.
  - fallback — starts on the first free numbered sibling of the profile
    (profiles/.../<name>-2 to -5) and reports the switch everywhere: that profile is
    NOT the profile you configured, it has separate cookies, logins and fingerprint seed,
    a sibling that did not exist is created empty and said to be empty, and when -2 to
    -5 are all in use no backend starts and the message names the owner.
  - isolated — starts with no profile at all: nothing is saved and nothing persists.
  - block — stops the backend and exposes only the broker meta-tools until Claude Code
    restarts the MCP server.

Default: copy

Notes:
  - Under profile_isolation copy and copy-keep the value means wait for the base, then
    take the copy, because a copy is never taken of a copy; those modes never fall back
    to a numbered sibling.
  - Only profiles the plugin manages are copied, given siblings or made isolated.
  - An explicit Profile directory keeps the block behaviour.
  - It has no effect on camoufox-native or kameleo, which manage their own profiles.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

copy_contents.title: Copy contents
copy_contents.description:
What a session copy of a browser profile holds.

Options:
  - identity — copies only the engine's identity core, as its manifest lists it:
    cookies, saved logins and the key that decrypts them, certificates, permissions
    and preferences, history and autofill, localStorage tokens, and the installed
    add-ons (their files travel together, never one without the others).
  - full — copies the whole profile plan: exactly the files and bytes 2.19.0 copied,
    including history, IndexedDB and caches.
    Measured on this machine: Firefox about 69 MB without add-ons and about 105 MB
    with them, Chromium about 28 MB, against 881 MB and 594 MB for full.

Default: identity

Notes:
  - It governs profile_isolation copy, on_locked copy and scripts/profile-copy.mjs
    alike, so the CLI and a session can never disagree.
  - Sites whose login lives in IndexedDB (WhatsApp Web, Google Drive, OneDrive, Notion
    and many PWAs) may ask you to sign in again with identity; a login kept in a cookie
    or in localStorage stays signed in.
  - profile_isolation copy-keep is always full whatever this says, because that session
    copy replaces the base profile on a clean close and a thinner tree would destroy
    the base's data; browser_capabilities reports copyContentsSource "clamped" with
    the reason.
  - A copy taken while another browser writes the profile can be a few seconds stale.
  - An engine whose manifest declares no identity list copies the full tree and says so.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

profile_lifetime.title: Profile lifetime
profile_lifetime.description:
How long this session keeps the profile facts it owns.

Options:
  - browser — takes the plugin's own lock on the base profile (profile_isolation copy
    and copy-keep) at the first browser action, releases it when the browser closes,
    and takes it again on the next browser action, so an idle Claude session locks and
    copies nothing and another session can take the profile as soon as your browser
    closes.
    A session copy taken for on_locked copy lives exactly as long: it is deleted when
    the browser closes (six bounded attempts over about 5 seconds), and a copy that
    still cannot be deleted is kept and reported as a leftover, never silently lost.
  - server — keeps the 2.19.0 behaviour: the lock and the copy last until the MCP
    server stops.

Default: browser

Notes:
  - One exception keeps the tool list usable: when this machine has no cached tool list
    yet for the engine, tool profile and tool groups in use, the copy (and the backend)
    is taken before the client asks for its tools, so the very first start of a new
    configuration locks and copies at start and every later session is lazy again.
  - It never changes the browser's own lock, which is always browser-scoped, or the
    bridge's lock, which stays server-scoped until an upstream release;
    browser_capabilities and browser_profiles report each lock's real lifetime and why.
  - copy-keep always keeps its copy until the session ends, because that copy carries
    your changes.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

seat_limit.title: CloakBrowser seat limit
seat_limit.description:
How many CloakBrowser browsers this machine may run at once, which decides whether
on_locked copy may start a browser on a copy while another session holds the profile.

Options:
  - engine-default — the engine's own rule: one concurrent browser on the free tier,
    exactly 2.19.0's behaviour.
  - unlimited — declares that your licence has no practical cap (Pro 200/2000+, or an
    older build that needs no key).
  - vendor-license — asks the vendor's licence API for the seats your key holds and
    uses its limit.
    That is a live network call to cloakbrowser.dev (10 second timeout) made only when
    a licence key is configured, and any failure falls back to the engine default and
    says so in browser_capabilities.

Default: engine-default

Notes:
  - Whatever the setting, the plugin always counts the live browser locks it can see in
    its own profile folders, and a launch the engine refuses with licence exit code 76
    to 79 is never retried in a loop.
  - When no seat is free, on_locked copy holds and retries instead of starting a second
    browser.
  - Only the cloakbrowser plugin declares this setting, because the camoufox plugin has
    no seat-limited engine.

Restart Claude Code after changing it.

identity_mode.title: Device identity (Camoufox)
identity_mode.description:
How the Camoufox engine presents its device identity.

Options:
  - profile — gives each persistent Camoufox profile one generated identity: the
    first launch draws a fingerprint for this computer's operating system, stores it
    in <profile>/.camoufox-identity.json and reuses it on every later launch, so a
    site that keeps cookies also sees the same device (Camoufox otherwise draws a
    new one on every launch).
  - random — restores the per-launch draw.

Default: profile

Notes:
  - Delete that file to draw a new identity on the next start; a copied profile
    carries it, so delete it inside the copy to give the copy a different device.
  - An isolated start has no profile to store anything in, so it always draws a new
    identity.
  - This setting is inert for the other engines: cloak pins its own Chromium seed,
    playwright and camoufox-native have no fingerprint input, and Kameleo manages
    its own profiles; browser_capabilities says so and reports the active source,
    the identity file and when it was created.

ping_timeout_ms.title: Server heartbeat timeout (Camoufox)
ping_timeout_ms.description:
How long the camoufox engine's backend waits for an answer to its own heartbeat
ping before it closes the browser and ends the session, in milliseconds.

Default: 0

Notes:
  - 0 disables the wrapper's heartbeat entirely.
  - The backend pings every 3 s and closes the browser when an answer is more than
    5 s late; one late answer (a stalled Claude Code event loop, a busy machine,
    sleep or resume) was enough to lose the browser, and a dead client is still
    detected through the MCP pipe itself.
  - A positive value re-enables the heartbeat with that deadline, so a client that
    does not answer within it still loses the browser and the session.
  - A non-negative integer; anything else is ignored with one log line and the
    heartbeat stays disabled.
  - The other engines send no server heartbeat and ignore this setting, and
    browser_capabilities and browser_engine_status say so.
  - An explicit PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_PING_TIMEOUT_MS in the environment wins over this
    setting.

password_manager.title: Saved logins and autofill (Camoufox)
password_manager.description:
Off by default. When on, Camoufox's Firefox password manager is enabled for this
profile: saved logins in the profile's logins.db can be autofilled into matching
login forms, and Firefox will offer to save new logins.

Notes:
  - This is a deliberate security trade-off. Autofilled credentials can be read by
    the page's own scripts, by the model through browser_snapshot or
    browser_evaluate, and by a prompt-injected page that steers the model to a login
    form; the plugin cannot tell a legitimate login page from a phishing one.
  - The store is encrypted with the profile's key4.db, which sits in the same profile
    and is not bound to your Windows account (no primary password is set by default):
    anyone who obtains the profile (a copy, a backup, profile_isolation=copy or
    copy-keep, or scripts/profile-copy.mjs) can decrypt the saved passwords.
  - Autofill on plain HTTP stays off, and address/credit-card autofill and form
    history stay off.
  - The pinned Camoufox build disables the manager by enterprise policy
    (PasswordManagerEnabled: false, OfferToSaveLogins: false), and launch prefs alone
    lose to that lock.
  - The camoufox engine always runs on a plugin-owned overlay of that build inside
    the plugin data directory (hardlinks and junctions to the build; only
    distribution/policies.json is replaced, every other policy preserved; about 0
    bytes on a normal install, about 310 MB only when the build cache is on another
    volume).
  - The overlay restores the stock search engines with Google as the default on
    every start; turning this setting on adds the two password policies and the
    three signon prefs to that same overlay, and turning it off removes only those.
  - It is verified once with a short headless start, and browser_capabilities
    reports the overlay directory, its mode and the policy path.
  - If the overlay cannot be created or verified, the stock build runs normally and
    browser_capabilities reports blocked-by-overlay with the reason; a directory
    this plugin did not write is never touched and reports blocked-by-existing-overlay.
  - Inert for cloak, playwright and kameleo; camoufox-native has no prefs input and
    reports native-unavailable.
  - The plugin never reads, logs or transmits logins.db or key4.db, and this setting
    never authorizes typing, submitting, recovering or handling 2FA or CAPTCHA on a
    credential form.

account.title: Account profile
account.description:
Browser profile name for one account. Each name keeps its own cookies, logins and
fingerprint seed under Claude Code's plugin data directory (profiles/<engine>/<name>).

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' only, starting with a letter or digit, up to
    64 characters, no trailing dot or space.
  - Leave empty to use the plugin's default profile (profiles/default).
  - Ignored when Persistent profile directory is set.
  - Changing it takes effect when the Claude Code MCP server restarts; sign in to
    each account manually in the headed window.

profile_dir.title: Persistent profile directory
profile_dir.description:
Directory that keeps cookies, logins and the fingerprint seed. It is created if it
does not exist.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty to use the plugin's own persistent profile in Claude Code's plugin
    data directory (profiles/default).
  - Use one directory per account.

proxy_server.title: Proxy server
proxy_server.description:
Sticky proxy URL, for example http://user:pass@host:port.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty for a direct connection.

proxy_bypass.title: Proxy bypass list
proxy_bypass.description:
Comma-separated hosts that should not use the proxy.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty to proxy everything.

licence_key.title: CloakBrowser licence key
licence_key.description:
CloakBrowser Pro licence key, held in the operating system credential
store.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - The free tier works without it and allows one concurrent session.

engine_version.title: Engine version pin
engine_version.description:
Pin a specific CloakBrowser Chromium build.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty to use the stable channel and let the binary update itself.

output_dir.title: Artifacts directory
output_dir.description:
Where Playwright MCP writes screenshots, traces and session files. It is created if it
does not exist.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Leave empty to write them to .playwright-mcp in the folder the client opened (its
    first file root), or, when the client advertises no usable file root, to the
    plugin data folder under output/<engine>.

allow_unrestricted_file_access.title: Unrestricted file access
allow_unrestricted_file_access.description:
Remove Playwright's file-access allowlist for tool-chosen paths and unblock file://
navigation, so the model can read and write any file your operating-system user can,
not only the Artifacts directory and the workspace root.

Default: false

Notes:
  - A deliberate security trade-off: a prompt-injected page could make the model
    read or overwrite private files.
  - Leave this off unless you need a path outside those roots.
  - Applies to the cloak, playwright, camoufox and kameleo engines; the
    camoufox-native engine has no file-path tools and ignores it.

extension_paths.title: Unpacked extensions
extension_paths.description:
Absolute directories of unpacked Chromium extensions to load in every start.

Default: empty

Notes:
  - Format: a JSON string array or a comma-separated list of absolute paths. Unpacked
    directories only: the Chrome Web Store is not available in this Chromium, and a
    directory cannot contain a comma.
  - Any and all extensions you list are allowed. An extension is privileged code that
    runs with the browser's privileges on every page and is outside the MCP tool
    filters: it bypasses disabled_tools, can read page content, cookies and storage,
    and can send that anywhere your network allows, so only load directories you
    trust.
  - There is no signature check at load and no automatic update.
  - Its stored data lives in the browser profile and therefore travels with profile copies,
    retained previous trees and backups.
  - Applies to the cloak engine only, which must run on a persistent profile: with
    profile_isolation isolated (or on_locked isolated) the server refuses to start
    until the extension list is cleared or a persistent profile mode is chosen.
  - While the list is set, only these directories are enabled, and any extension you
    installed by hand in the profile stays disabled for that start.
  - In shared, workspace and account profiles the extension state persists;
    profile_isolation copy discards a session's extension changes when it ends cleanly,
    and copy-keep keeps them by swapping the session copy into the base.
  - The other engines ignore the setting and say so in browser_capabilities.
  - An explicit CLOAK_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXTENSION_PATHS in the environment wins over this
    setting.
